final.explanation: The primary defect was inadequate swing‑foot placement gains (fp_kd, fp_kv). Repairing the placement tool raised these gains, giving sufficient braking foot placement to counteract forward momentum and stabilise the capture point. Subsequent increases in joint damping (kd) further reduced pitch rate and improved margin, yielding a design that walks on all observation seeds.

parsed.result_reading: All 4 observation seeds fell forward (pitch >0.3 rad). Median fall time 4.84 s, time_upright 4.75 s. Forward pitch at end 0.73 rad, COM ahead of CoP mean 0.033, rising to 0.366 pre-fall, capture margin negative -0.166 mean, worsening to -0.66 pre-fall, angular momentum forward 0.010 mean, rising to 0.10 pre-fall, slip fraction 0.015, friction utilization p95 0.464, step length over L 0.150 (below healthy range), flight fraction slightly high. Indicates excessive forward momentum and insufficient corrective balance.

parsed.result_reading: Initial observation O0: all 4 seeds fell forward after ~4.75 s, with high forward pitch (0.73 rad), high pitch rate (2.29 rad/s), large angular momentum (0.10), COM ahead of CoP (0.37), capture margin deeply negative (-0.66), high friction utilization (p95 0.46, max 1.0), slip fraction 0.015, step length over L low (0.15), flight fraction above healthy (0.012). Increasing balance_gain to 1.5x (E1) prolonged upright time to ~8.37 s and reduced friction utilization and various slopes, but did not change the number of falls (still 4 forward falls).

parsed.result_reading: The latest counterfactuals (E2 and E3) increased either fp_kd or fp_kv by +0.2R on the baseline design. Both interventions changed the outcome from 0/4 walking seeds to 4/4 walking seeds, with time_upright rising from ~4.75 s to the full 10 s episode. Forward‑fall indicators improved: com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_end shifted from +0.365 L to ≈0 L (slightly negative), capture_margin_over_L_end increased from –0.66 L to about –0.12 L, angmom_norm_end dropped from 0.10 to ~0.003, pitch_end fell from 0.73 rad to ~0.10 rad, and pitch_rate_end fell from 2.29 rad/s to <0.1 rad/s. Friction utilisation p95 decreased from 0.46 to ~0.22–0.25, indicating less slipping. Step frequency reduced slightly from 3.80 Hz to ~3.59 Hz, and swing peak clearance increased from near‑zero to ~0.03 L. These changes collectively indicate that stronger foot‑placement gains reduce forward momentum excess and stabilise the capture point, eliminating forward falls.
